steps.body: A line is the friendliest arrangement to count: start at one end, touch each thing in turn, and stop at the other end.
steps.narration: A line is the friendliest arrangement to count: start at one end, touch each thing in turn, and stop at the other end.

widget.prompt: Start at 5. Hop forward 4 times by 1. Where do you land?

commonLandings.feedback: 8 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 9.
10 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 4 hops from 5 to land on 9.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 5 and count on 4: you land on 9.
widget.successFeedback: 5 and 4 more is 9 — each hop says the next counting number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — count all 4 hops, one number per hop, to reach 9.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after exactly 4 hops, on 9.

predict.prompt: Counting a line of things, where do you start?
predict.reveal: Starting at an end keeps counted and uncounted things on opposite sides of your finger — start in the middle and uncounted things sit on both sides, easy to skip or count twice.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch count line.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch count line.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: Kai counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 3, tells how many blocks there are in all.
The count stops at 3; saying one more number would count a block that is not there.
That stops one number early — every block gets exactly one number, ending at 3.
That runs two past the count; the last number spoken is the answer, and it was 3.
